slot.brief: Rank bond order/bond length of a given bond (e.g. C–O or N–O) across a molecule and its resonance-related ions; ask for the correct increasing bond-length order.

stem: Which is the increasing order of average N–O bond lengths in $\text{NO}_2^+$, $\text{NO}_2^-$ and $\text{NO}_3^-$?

verdicts.working: Resonance gives average N–O bond orders of 2 in NO₂⁺, 1.5 in NO₂⁻, and 4/3 in NO₃⁻. Lower bond order corresponds to greater bond length, so the increasing order is NO₂⁺ < NO₂⁻ < NO₃⁻.

working:
Average N–O bond orders: $\text{NO}_2^+=2$; $\text{NO}_2^-=1.5$; $\text{NO}_3^-=\dfrac{4}{3}$.\nBond length decreases as bond order increases.\nThus: $\text{NO}_2^+ < \text{NO}_2^- < \text{NO}_3^-$.

Independent check: Resonance gives average N–O bond orders of 2 in NO₂⁺, 1.5 in NO₂⁻, and 4/3 in NO₃⁻. Lower bond order corresponds to greater bond length, so the increasing order is NO₂⁺ < NO₂⁻ < NO₃⁻.
solution:
Resonance gives average N–O bond orders of $2$, $1.5$, and $\frac{4}{3}$ in $\text{NO}_2^+$, $\text{NO}_2^-$, and $\text{NO}_3^-$, respectively. Since bond length decreases as bond order increases,
$$\text{NO}_2^+ < \text{NO}_2^- < \text{NO}_3^-$$
